text:
Simon Holmstrom used to be the Islanders' useful third-liner. Over the last ten games he has played 20 minutes a night, more than four minutes above where he was, and he is now on the ice for 48% of their power-play chances after 19% last season. At 25, that is a real promotion, and it is why our numbers flag him as a breakout.

The production is steady rather than spectacular: ten points in 17 games, with five goals on 4.92 expected. No luck to strip out there. He is getting to better ice, 0.94 expected goals per 60 against 0.66 last season.

What makes the minutes make sense is the 5v5 picture. With him on the ice the Islanders have 53% of expected goals, four points better than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 57% of his entries, and Evolving-Hockey credited him with drawing more penalties than he takes.

The test now is whether the bigger role holds through the Islanders' three straight overtime losses and whatever changes come with them.
headline: Holmstrom earns 20 minutes on Long Island
